title: Joe Kelly's band and the Gaslight Club

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did John Board come in?
John Board came in, I think, about two, three years, now.
He's a good tenor man.
He's a good tenor man.
I think I first heard him when he was with Hampton, a long time ago.

And after the -- we left the Gaslight and we worked a lot of jobs around town, like the Raw Onion. And Big John's Distillery, and Captain's House, and The Hanger, out in -- out west here in town, out west here, right at the toll road. Can't think of the name of the town --
suburb.
Addison?
No, it wasn't Addison.
Well, then you went back into the Gaslight?
Then we went back into the Gaslight. After we went back in the Gaslight that time, we stayed there.
What does that band play, mostly, at the Gaslight?
Well, what we call Chicago jazz. Wasn't Dixieland.
More swing?
More swing, like the Chicago, Chicago jazz.
Hard driving?
Hard driving.
Mostly four-beat?
Yeah, mostly four-beat. More than two.
When did Barrett leave?
Barrett left -- when we left the Gaslight, Barrett stayed in the Gaslight.
Oh, that's right, he'd been hired separately.
He was hired separate. He stayed in the Gaslight when we left.
I remember it. And he started using Johnny Board, I recall while, ...to get it correct in my mind. I know he told me about it. He had a trio, I think. Maybe quartet.
I can't remember exactly.
Different people were there, I think. The trombone player was --
Yeah, because Barrett stayed with all the different bands that was there.
Complaining all the way.
Yeah.
